# Implementation Plan: Calculator View Modes + GitHub Pages Deployment

**Branch**: `001-calc-view-modes` | **Date**: 2026-05-15 | **Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-calc-view-modes/spec.md`
**Amendment**: User input — "add a github pages entry to deploy it."

**Note**: This plan was regenerated by `/speckit-plan` to incorporate the GitHub Pages deployment addition. Core calculator implementation is already complete; this plan covers the deployment layer only.

## Summary

The calculator (vanilla HTML/CSS/ES2020 JS, zero dependencies) is already implemented and tested. This plan adds a GitHub Pages deployment job to the existing CI workflow so that every merge to `main` automatically publishes the live calculator at the repository's GitHub Pages URL. No build step is required — the static files are uploaded directly as a Pages artifact.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: HTML5, CSS3, ES2020+ (vanilla JS — no transpilation, no bundler)

**Primary Dependencies**: None (Zero-dependency per Constitution Principle I). CI uses official GitHub Actions only — these are runner infrastructure, not code dependencies.

**Storage**: N/A (client-side only)

**Testing**: Custom in-repo test harness (`tests/harness.js`, Node 22-compatible). No new tests required for CI/CD infrastructure.

**Target Platform**: GitHub Pages (static hosting); same modern browsers as before.

**Project Type**: Static web application deployed via GitHub Pages

**Performance Goals**: Deploy completes within the GitHub Actions free-tier time limit (typically < 2 minutes for a static upload).

**Constraints**: WCAG 2.1 AA (unchanged), no build step, no external services, CI must run without secrets. GitHub Pages requires `pages: write` and `id-token: write` OIDC permissions — no PAT needed.

**Scale/Scope**: One new job added to `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. No source file changes.

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

| Gate | Principle | Status | Notes |
|------|-----------|--------|-------|
| I | Zero-dependency plain web stack | **PASS** | Official GitHub Actions (`actions/configure-pages`, `actions/upload-pages-artifact`, `actions/deploy-pages`) are CI runner tools, not code dependencies — they do not enter the shipped artefact |
| II | Minimal token/code footprint | **PASS** | One new `deploy` job in the existing workflow file; no new source files, no new abstractions |
| III | Test-driven development | **PASS** | No new calculator logic → no new tests required. The existing test suite continues to gate deployment (deploy job `needs: test`) |
| IV | CI via GitHub Actions | **PASS** | Deployment is implemented inside GitHub Actions, fully satisfying the CI requirement |

*Post-design re-check: All gates remain PASS. No constitution violations.*

## Workflow Design

### Updated `.github/workflows/ci.yml` structure

```yaml
jobs:
  test:          # existing — syntax check + node tests/run.js
  deploy:        # NEW — runs only on push to main, needs: test
    permissions:
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      - checkout
      - configure-pages
      - upload-pages-artifact (path: '.')
      - deploy-pages
```

**Guard**: `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'` — deploy runs only on merges to main, never on PRs.

**Artifact path**: `.` (repo root) — GitHub Pages serves `index.html` directly. The `_config.yml` exclusion is not needed because the project has no Jekyll files.
